question.text: A tangent is drawn to the parabola <math><msup><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn><mi>x</mi></math> at <math><mi>P</mi><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal"></mi><mn>4</mn></mrow></mfenced></math> to intersect the <math><mi>x</mi></math>-axis at <math><mi>Q</mi><mo>,</mo></math> from which another tangent is drawn to the parabola to touch it at <math><mi>R</mi><mo>.</mo></math> If the normal at <math><mi>R</mi></math> intersects the parabola again at <math><mi>S</mi><mo>,</mo></math> then the coordinates of <math><mi>S</mi></math> are

solution.text:
P is one of the end points of the latus rectum.

So, Q lies on the directrix.
Hence, R=2,-4.
Equation of the normal at R is y=x-6
⇒S=18,12
